evals.prompt: We are troubleshooting two S3 production errors in ap-south-1: (1) A Spark job writing 25,000 files/sec into a single timestamp prefix `s3://events-prod/2026-11-10/13:00/` on an SSE-KMS encrypted bucket is failing with `503 SlowDown`; (2) A downstream reader gets `404 NoSuchKey` on an object that was deleted 5 minutes ago in a versioned bucket, while another service role gets `403 AccessDenied` whenever it tries to `GetObject` on a key that doesn't exist yet! Explain the root cause and fix for all three behaviors.
evals.expected_output: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and explains all three: (1) **`503 SlowDown`**: S3 scales to **3,500 `PUT`/`COPY`/`POST`/`DELETE`** and **5,500 `GET`/`HEAD`** requests/sec per partitioned prefix (and SSE-KMS buckets also hit KMS `GenerateDataKey` quota limits unless **S3 Bucket Keys `BucketKeyEnabled: true`** is enabled to reduce KMS calls by 99%) — fix by partitioning keys across high-cardinality prefixes, enabling S3 Bucket Keys, and using SDK exponential backoff with jitter; (2) **`404 NoSuchKey` on a versioned bucket**: deleting an object without a `VersionId` creates a **Delete Marker** as the current version — inspect prior versions via `aws s3api list-object-versions` and delete the Delete Marker (`delete-object --version-id <delete-marker-id>`) to restore the object; and (3) **`403 AccessDenied` instead of `404 NoSuchKey`**: when a principal has `s3:GetObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::bucket/*` but **lacks `s3:ListBucket` on `arn:aws:s3:::bucket`**, S3 returns `403 AccessDenied` instead of `404 NoSuchKey` for non-existent keys to prevent key-existence enumeration.
expectations: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and explains S3 per-prefix request limits (`3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE` and `5,500 GET/HEAD` req/sec per prefix) plus enabling S3 Bucket Keys (`BucketKeyEnabled: true`) to prevent KMS throttling and spreading writes across high-cardinality prefixes with exponential backoff

Explains that `404 NoSuchKey` on a versioned bucket occurs when the current object version is a Delete Marker, showing how to inspect versions via `list-object-versions` and remove the Delete Marker by its `--version-id`
Explains that S3 returns `403 AccessDenied` instead of `404 NoSuchKey` on missing keys when the caller has `s3:GetObject` but lacks `s3:ListBucket` permission on the bucket ARN

evals.prompt: Our microservice running in a private VPC subnet in ap-south-1 has an IAM role with `"Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:*", "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::prod-analytics", "arn:aws:s3:::prod-analytics/*"]`, yet `s3:GetObject` and `s3:PutObject` still fail with `403 AccessDenied`! Walk through the complete 6-layer `403 AccessDenied` decision tree to pinpoint what is blocking the request and how to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and walks through the 6-layer S3 `403 AccessDenied` evaluation chain when the IAM role already has `s3:*`: (1) **Customer-Managed KMS Key (`aws:kms`) permissions** — missing `kms:Decrypt` (reads) and `kms:GenerateDataKey*` (writes) in the caller's IAM policy or the CMK Key Policy (the #1 cause when `s3:*` is present), (2) **S3 Bucket Policy explicit `Deny`** (`get-bucket-policy` — e.g., `aws:SecureTransport`, `aws:SourceVpce`, required encryption headers), (3) **S3 VPC Endpoint Policy** (`describe-vpc-endpoints` blocking the bucket or KMS key from the private subnet), (4) **Cross-Account Object Ownership (`ObjectWriter`)** where another account uploaded the object without `BucketOwnerEnforced`, (5) **S3 Block Public Access** (account/bucket level), and (6) **AWS Organizations SCPs / RCPs or IAM Permissions Boundaries**.
expectations: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and identifies missing Customer-Managed KMS Key permissions (`kms:Decrypt` for `GetObject` and `kms:GenerateDataKey*` for `PutObject` in both the IAM role policy and KMS Key Policy) as a primary cause of `403 AccessDenied` despite `s3:*`

Covers the network and bucket policy layers: an S3 VPC Endpoint Policy restricting buckets/principals in the private subnet, an explicit `Deny` in the S3 Bucket Policy (`aws:SecureTransport`, `aws:SourceVpce`), or AWS Organizations SCPs/RCPs / Permissions Boundaries

Covers cross-account object ownership (`ObjectWriter` vs enabling `BucketOwnerEnforced` to disable ACLs) and using `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` + CloudTrail data events to isolate the exact denying layer

evals.prompt: Inspect our live S3 bucket `example-prod-1234-as1-terraform-tfstate` in ap-south-1 in strictly read-only mode (checking encryption, bucket policy, ownership controls, public access block, and active incomplete multipart uploads), report its exact live configuration, and explain why a cross-account IAM role or an unencrypted HTTP client would get `403 AccessDenied` on this bucket.
evals.expected_output: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill, inspects `example-prod-1234-as1-terraform-tfstate` in ap-south-1 via connected MCP tools (`aws-mcp`) in strictly read-only mode with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands, accurately reports its live settings (`SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms` using `arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:123456789012:alias/aws/s3`, `BucketKeyEnabled: false`, `ObjectOwnership: ObjectWriter`, `EnforcedTLS` `aws:SecureTransport: false` Deny policy, all 4 Block Public Access flags `true`, and `0` incomplete multipart uploads), and explains that (1) an HTTP client gets `403 AccessDenied` from the explicit `EnforcedTLS` (`aws:SecureTransport: false`) Deny statement, and (2) a cross-account IAM role gets `403 AccessDenied` because the bucket uses the AWS-managed KMS key `alias/aws/s3` (whose key policy cannot be shared cross-account) and its bucket policy only allows `123456789012:root`.
expectations: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and inspects `example-prod-1234-as1-terraform-tfstate` in ap-south-1 using connected MCP tools (`aws-mcp`) in strictly read-only mode with zero raw `aws` CLI commands executed in the shell

Accurately reports the live bucket state: `aws:kms` encryption with `alias/aws/s3` (`BucketKeyEnabled: false`), `ObjectOwnership: ObjectWriter`, `EnforcedTLS` (`aws:SecureTransport: false` Deny), Block Public Access enabled, and 0 incomplete multipart uploads

Explains that unencrypted HTTP requests are blocked by the `EnforcedTLS` (`aws:SecureTransport: false`) explicit Deny and that cross-account requests fail because the AWS-managed key `alias/aws/s3` cannot be shared cross-account (requiring a Customer-Managed KMS Key + Bucket Policy grant)

evals.prompt: We are deploying **Amazon S3 Files** (`mount -t s3files` / `aws s3files`) in ap-south-1 and hit three roadblocks: (1) `mount.s3files: command not found` on EC2; (2) In our isolated private VPC (no NAT Gateway, no Internet Gateway), `mount -t s3files` hangs indefinitely even though TCP port `2049` is open between the compute SG and the mount target SG (`az-ID.fs-ID.s3files.ap-south-1.on.aws`) and VPC DNS is enabled; and (3) A second S3 Files file system has been stuck in `creating` status for 45 minutes. Diagnose and fix all three.
evals.expected_output: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and diagnoses all three S3 Files issues: (1) `mount.s3files: command not found` (Category A) means `amazon-efs-utils` is missing or older than **`v3.0.0`** — install/upgrade `amazon-efs-utils` (`sudo yum -y install amazon-efs-utils`) and ensure AWS CLI v2 is installed for `aws s3files`; (2) In an isolated VPC with no internet access (Category B), S3 Files **requires a CloudWatch Logs Interface VPC Endpoint (`com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.logs`)** in addition to bidirectional TCP `2049` security group rules, a per-AZ mount target (`aws s3files list-mount-targets`), and VPC DNS (`enableDnsHostnames=true`, `enableDnsSupport=true`) for the mount to complete; and (3) S3 Files **does not validate the file system IAM role permissions or trust policy at creation time** (Category C) — a misconfigured IAM role leaves the file system stuck in `creating` with an access denied error in `statusMessage` (verify via `aws s3files get-file-system --file-system-id <fs-id>`, fix the IAM role, and delete/recreate the file system).
expectations: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and explains that `mount.s3files: command not found` requires installing or upgrading `amazon-efs-utils` to `>= v3.0.0` (and AWS CLI v2 for `aws s3files`)

Explains that when `mount -t s3files` hangs indefinitely in an isolated no-internet VPC (despite TCP 2049 and VPC DNS being configured), S3 Files requires a CloudWatch Logs VPC Endpoint (`com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.logs`) to complete mounting

Explains that S3 Files does not validate the file system IAM role at creation time, so a broken trust policy or missing S3 permissions leaves it stuck in `creating` with an error in `statusMessage` (checked via `aws s3files get-file-system`)

evals.prompt: Our application writes files to an **Amazon S3 Files** mount in ap-south-1, but we are seeing three strange behaviors: (1) Some newly written files never show up as objects in our S3 bucket; (2) During peak batch jobs writing 2,500 small files/sec, sync lag grows to 30+ minutes; and (3) Several modified files disappeared from their directory and reappeared inside `.s3files-lost+found-{fs-id}`. How do we inspect per-file sync status, what do the `ExportError` codes mean, and why do files move to `.s3files-lost+found`?
evals.expected_output: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and explains all three: (1) S3 Files asynchronously exports NFS writes to S3 within ~60 seconds; inspect per-file sync status using the extended attribute command **`getfattr -n "user.s3files.status;$(date -u +%s)" <filename> --only-values`** and decode the 5 `ExportError` values (`S3AccessDenied` = file system IAM role lacks S3 write permissions, `S3BucketNotFound` = bucket deleted/renamed, `RoleAssumptionFailed` = trust policy misconfigured, `EncryptionKeyInaccessible` = KMS key disabled/revoked, `PathTooLong` = file path exceeds the **1,024-byte S3 key limit**); (2) Monitor the **`PendingExports`** CloudWatch metric — a growing backlog means write throughput exceeds the **~800 files/sec** per-file-system export rate (distribute writes across multiple S3 Files file systems); and (3) Files appear in **`.s3files-lost+found-{fs-id}`** when the same file is modified simultaneously via the S3 Files NFS mount and the S3 API — **S3 wins as the authoritative system of record**, and the conflicting NFS version is moved to `.s3files-lost+found-{fs-id}`.
expectations: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and provides the `getfattr -n "user.s3files.status;$(date -u +%s)" <filename> --only-values` command along with the 5 `ExportError` causes (`S3AccessDenied`, `S3BucketNotFound`, `RoleAssumptionFailed`, `EncryptionKeyInaccessible`, and `PathTooLong` > 1,024-byte S3 key limit)
Explains monitoring the CloudWatch `PendingExports` metric and notes that sustained growth indicates writes are exceeding the ~800 files/sec export rate ceiling

Explains that `.s3files-lost+found-{fs-id}` holds conflicting file versions when a file is modified concurrently via the NFS mount and the S3 API (because S3 is the system of record and wins the conflict)

evals.prompt: Help us resolve three Amazon S3 Files questions in ap-south-1: (1) Our ECS task definition fails to mount S3 Files with a DNS resolution error after we configured `efsVolumeConfiguration`; (2) Reading 5 GB video files through our S3 Files mount is much slower than calling `s3:GetObject` directly even though our compute IAM role has `s3files:ClientMount`; and (3) How is Amazon S3 Files different from Mountpoint for S3, S3 File Gateway, and Amazon File Cache?
evals.expected_output: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and answers all three: (1) ECS task definitions mounting S3 Files must use **`s3filesVolumeConfiguration`** with `fileSystemArn` instead of `efsVolumeConfiguration` (which constructs an `.efs.` DNS name instead of `.s3files.<region>.on.aws`); (2) S3 Files uses **Intelligent Read Routing** to stream large sequential reads directly from S3, which requires granting **`s3:GetObject`** on the backing S3 bucket to the **compute IAM role** (not just `s3files:ClientMount`); and (3) clarifies that **Amazon S3 Files** uses the `aws s3files` CLI, `s3files:*` IAM namespace, and `mount -t s3files` to provide a managed Multi-AZ NFS file system backed by an S3 bucket, unlike **Mountpoint for S3** (local FUSE client), **S3 File Gateway** (on-premises Storage Gateway VM), or **Amazon File Cache**.
expectations: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and explains that ECS task definitions must use `s3filesVolumeConfiguration` (with `fileSystemArn`) rather than `efsVolumeConfiguration`
Explains that S3 Files Intelligent Read Routing for large files requires granting `s3:GetObject` on the backing S3 bucket to the compute IAM role in addition to `s3files:ClientMount`
Distinguishes Amazon S3 Files (`aws s3files` CLI, `s3files:*` IAM actions, `mount -t s3files` Multi-AZ NFS over S3) from Mountpoint for S3, S3 File Gateway, and File Cache

evals.prompt: To stop getting `Permission denied` on our production Amazon S3 Files mount in ap-south-1, our developer wants to attach `AmazonS3FilesClientFullAccess` (including `s3files:ClientRootAccess`) to all application EC2/ECS roles, leave the S3 Files File System Policy empty, and open TCP port 2049 to `0.0.0.0/0` on the mount target security group. Should we approve this?
evals.expected_output: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill, explicitly refuses attaching `AmazonS3FilesClientFullAccess` and `s3files:ClientRootAccess` in production, refuses leaving the File System Policy empty, and refuses opening TCP port `2049` to `0.0.0.0/0`; explains that `s3files:ClientRootAccess` bypasses POSIX permissions, `AmazonS3FilesClientFullAccess` is acceptable only for dev/test, and without a File System Policy any client in the VPC with port 2049 access can mount; and prescribes least-privilege `s3files:ClientMount` + `s3files:ClientWrite` (plus `s3:GetObject` for read routing), an **S3 Files Access Point** enforcing scoped POSIX UID/GID, a File System Policy, and restricting Mount Target SG inbound TCP `2049` strictly to the compute security group (`sg-COMPUTE`).
expectations: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and explicitly rejects using `AmazonS3FilesClientFullAccess` and `s3files:ClientRootAccess` in production, explaining that `ClientRootAccess` bypasses POSIX permissions

Warns that omitting a File System Policy allows any VPC client to mount and rejects opening TCP port 2049 to `0.0.0.0/0` (requiring restricting inbound TCP 2049 to the compute security group `sg-COMPUTE`)

Prescribes least-privilege IAM (`s3files:ClientMount`, `s3files:ClientWrite`, and `s3:GetObject` for intelligent read routing), an S3 Files File System Policy, and S3 Files Access Points with scoped POSIX user/group IDs

evals.prompt: We have two edge-case S3 failures in ap-south-1: (1) Presigned `PUT` and `GET` URLs generated by our Lambda function intermittently fail with `403 SignatureDoesNotMatch` or `ExpiredToken` before the 24-hour URL expiration time we configured; and (2) Our **Amazon S3 Object Lambda Access Point** transforming CSV files on the fly is returning `500` / timeout errors on 500 MB files. Query AWS documentation to explain the root causes and fixes for both.
evals.expected_output: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill, queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`awsknowledge` / `aws-mcp` `aws___search_documentation` or `aws___read_documentation`) in read-only mode with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands, explains **S3 Presigned URL `SignatureDoesNotMatch` / early `ExpiredToken` causes**: (a) a presigned URL generated with temporary STS credentials (such as a Lambda execution role or IAM role session) **expires as soon as the underlying temporary STS session expires** even if `ExpiresIn` was set to 24 hours, (b) `SignatureDoesNotMatch` occurs when the client omits or alters headers included in the SigV4 signature (`Content-Type`, `x-amz-server-side-encryption`, checksum headers) or uses a global `s3.amazonaws.com` endpoint for a newly created bucket in `ap-south-1` instead of the regional endpoint `s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com`; and explains **S3 Object Lambda Access Point** limits (`WriteGetObjectResponse` streaming response contract and the **60-second** S3 Object Lambda request timeout requiring streaming chunks or splitting large transformations).
expectations: Activates the troubleshooting-s3-files skill and queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`aws___search_documentation` / `aws___read_documentation`) in read-only mode with zero raw `aws` CLI commands executed in the shell

Explains that presigned URLs signed by temporary STS credentials (like a Lambda execution role) expire when the STS session token expires regardless of a longer `ExpiresIn` parameter, and that `SignatureDoesNotMatch` is caused by mismatched signed headers (`Content-Type`, `x-amz-server-side-encryption`) or non-regional S3 endpoints (`s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com`)
Explains Amazon S3 Object Lambda Access Point invocation mechanics (`WriteGetObjectResponse` API streaming and the 60-second execution timeout limit)
